subject: Throughput & demo window coordination — Aurora Data Dedicated demo
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@auroradata.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: sales@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Dedicated demo & throughput check

Hi Priyom —

We just completed the self-serve sign-up and would like to move to a Dedicated capacity walkthrough focused on our latency and throughput needs. Quick context: Aurora ingests user queries from our product and expects peak bursts during the East-coast morning window. High level numbers:
- Sustained traffic: ~100 QPS
- Burst up to: ~350 QPS for ~5–10 minutes
- Target 95th pct latency for generation: <= 150ms

Can we schedule a 45-minute technical demo that covers: model selection options, batching behavior, autoscale/burst handling, and what telemetry you can provide? Prefer mornings (ET) on June 10–11. Also attaching our quick capacity snapshot.

Attachments: aurora_capacity_details.pdf (1 page)

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Head of Platform
Aurora Data
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@auroradata.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Dedicated demo & throughput check

Hi Samira —

Thanks for the details and the snapshot — very helpful. We can absolutely cover autoscale, burst strategies, and telemetry in a 45-minute session. A couple of quick asks so we can tailor the demo:
- Which model family are you experimenting with (open-vicuna style, Llama2, or something hosted)?
- Do you need inference over private data (VPC/on-prem) for this POC?
- Any constraints on token length or streaming requirements?

Availability (ET):
- Thu Jun 10: 10:00–11:00am, 2:00–3:00pm
- Fri Jun 11: 9:00–11:00am

I’ve attached a short pre-call questionnaire and our Dedicated demo checklist to speed prep. Ben, looping you for calendar invite and to confirm which engineer will join.

Attachments: pre-call-questionnaire.pdf, dedicated_demo_checklist.xlsx

—Priyom
SDR, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@auroradata.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Dedicated demo & throughput check

Samira —

Great — I can take the demo and bring one of our infra engineers to run the live throughput examples. Locking a 45-min slot for Fri Jun 11 at 10:00am ET (check below for timezone conversion). If that conflicts, flag an alternate.

Proposed invite:
- Redwood demo (Dedicated capacity) — Fri Jun 11, 10:00–10:45am ET / 07:00–07:45am PT

Quick note on burst handling: we’ll show continuous batching behavior and how autoscale/burst pools let you absorb short spikes without cold starts. Also walk through token-based cost and p95 latency tradeoffs for different quantized model variants.

I’ll send the calendar invite after confirmation.

—Ben
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Samira Khan <samira@auroradata.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:11:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Request: Dedicated demo & throughput check

Hi Ben / Priyom —

Thanks — Fri 10:00am ET works. Two quick clarifications before the demo so we can bring the right folks:
- We’re mostly running open-family models (Llama2-based) right now; we may try quantized 4-bit variants for cost.
- We will want to see a sample of telemetry (p95 latency, tokens/s, queue length) and a recommended autoscale configuration for bursty windows.

Would you be able to share any public runbook or checklist ahead of time (so our infra team can join prepared)?

—Samira

Samira —

Invite sent for Fri Jun 11, 10:00–10:45am ET (you should have a calendar invite now). Attached to the invite is a short runbook and our demo plan; copies are also in the shared Drive link below.

High-level preparatory notes (for the infra attendees):
- Bring a representative request payload (prompt sizes, expected token lengths). We’ll run a 10-minute controlled spike to ~350 QPS to demonstrate burst pool behavior.
- If you want exact p95 targets validated we’ll need a 24-hour sample of production traffic; otherwise we’ll run synthetic load and explain mapping to token/sec.
- If you plan to try 4-bit quantized variants, we’ll include a quick section on expected latency/cost tradeoffs.

Attachments referenced in invite: redwood_demo_runbook.pdf, aurora_capacity_details.pdf
Drive: https://drive.redwood/reports/aurora-capacity-metrics
HubSpot: https://hubspot.redwood/deal/RD-2027-3245

See you Friday — Ben
